analysis: Q2 reveals fundamentally different backbones: Heath constructs pentagons on the twelve edges of the cube by erecting perpendiculars (RU, SV, TW) from the cube's planes and uses 6.32 to prove coplanarity, 13.5 to establish further golden-ratio relationships for equiangularity, and 13.7 to conclude equiangularity from three equal angles. The AI instead constructs pentagons on the six faces of the cube via golden-section divisions of half-edges, then forms six bridging pentagons across adjacent faces, using 13.8 and symmetry arguments for regularity and 13.1/13.3 for the circumscription computation. These are genuinely different construction strategies, not mere citation-depth differences. The heath_only citations (6.32, 11.1, 11.6, 13.5, 13.7, 5.15) are not subsumed by any single higher-level AI citation but reflect Heath's distinct edge-based construction approach. Under Q3, the AI's different path is logically valid under the hardened 1(b) standard: it cites propositions for its key claims (1.4, 1.8 for congruence, 13.1/13.4 for golden-ratio identities, 13.6 for the apotome conclusion), and while terse and summary-style in places, no positively identifiable defect from the closed list of five error modes can be established.
